To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NDV grown in monolayers is larger and has more fragile envelope than NDV grown in embryonated egg, but both NDV grown in either way contain multiploid virion.
NDV virions grown in monolayers differ in morphology from virions grown in eggs and that this is due to a host cell effect.
the morphological heterogeneity of NDV is due to differences in host cell and that the differences are not due to differences in virion clumping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the morphologic, biophysical, and genetic differences between NDV populations propagated in embryonating chicken eggs and in monolayers.
the characterization of the morphologic heterogeneity of NDV propagated in two different hosts.
the characterization of NDV virions produced in embryonated chicken eggs (E- and M-), and in chick embryo fibroblast monolayers (M-), with respect to size, density, and morphology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E- and M-propagated NDV are different in size, buoyant density, sedimentation rate, and stability.

the morphologic heterogeneity observed in E- and M-propagated NDV virions is not the result of the presence of a single contaminant virus, but is the result of the growth of a heterogeneous population of virions.
M-NDV virion populations are morphologically and physically heterogeneous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the morphologic and biochemical heterogeneity of NDV is a reflection of the genetic heterogeneity of the virus.
E-NDV is a more stable virus and that M-NDV is more fragile.

the morphologic and biophysical differences observed between the E- and M-propagated NDV are not due to the presence of contaminating virions, clumping of virions, or differences in growth media, and that the differences are host controlled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of NDV virions is influenced by the host cell in which the virus is grown.
the morphologic heterogeneity of NDV virions is host dependent, and this heterogeneity can be propagated indefinitely in monolayers.
the virus that is isolated in the lab is not necessarily the virus that is circulating in the field.
